extra.message: User-controlled 'search' query parameter (request.args.get('search')) is interpolated directly into a SQL query via f-string at line 137 and executed at line 138 (cursor.execute(s_query)). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. ' OR '1'='1) to dump or manipulate the database.

file.filename from the multipart upload is used unsanitized in os.path.join(UPLOAD_FOLDER, filename) and saved with file.save(). A filename like '../../evil.py' allows writing arbitrary files outside the uploads directory (path traversal / arbitrary file write). werkzeug.utils.secure_filename is never used.

update_profile() trusts 'role' and 'permissions' submitted in the POST form (request.form['role'] / request.form['permissions']) and writes them to the users table at lines 229-234. Any authenticated user can escalate privileges by submitting role=admin&permissions=all. The commented-out code shows the sensitive fields were meant to be excluded.

GET /api/v1/profile has its @token_required decorator commented out (lines 152-153) and returns username, email, role, permissions and team for any user_id supplied in the query string. Unauthenticated attackers can enumerate and read every user's profile (IDOR / missing authentication).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: DELETE /api/v1/delete-user/<user_id> performs no authentication or authorization (@token_required commented out at line 221) and deletes any user account by ID. The endpoint's own docstring states it lacks proper authorization checks. Any unauthenticated attacker can delete arbitrary users (Broken Function Level Authorization).

POST /api/v1/update_picture passes the user-supplied 'picture_url' directly to requests.get() with no validation or allowlist, and the response body is written to disk. Attackers can make the server issue requests to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints (SSRF).

POST /api/v1/update_picture has no authentication (no token_required, no session check) and takes 'username' from the request payload, allowing any unauthenticated attacker to modify any user's profile picture (broken object-level authorization / IDOR).

extra.message: The /uploads/profile_pictures/<filename> route serves uploaded profile pictures with no session check (unlike /uploads/<filename>), exposing user-uploaded files to unauthenticated users.

extra.message: The 'search' query parameter is passed from server/routes.py:143 into the template and rendered with the '| safe' filter, disabling Jinja2 autoescaping. A crafted URL such as /dashboard?search="><script>alert(1)</script> executes JavaScript in the victim's browser (reflected XSS).
user.country is rendered with '| safe'. Country is attacker-controlled via /signup and /update_profile, so a stored XSS payload saved as the country executes whenever the profile page is viewed.

custom_hash() hashes passwords with unsalted MD5 (hashlib.md5), used for both registration (line 93) and login verification (line 50, api_v1.py:127). MD5 is fast and broken, making stored password hashes trivially crackable.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'just_another_secret'. It protects Flask session cookies and signs JWTs (api_v1.py:94, 133). Anyone with source access can forge sessions and JWT tokens, bypassing API authentication.

DEBUG = True is set in the committed config and passed to app.run(debug=...) in run.py:10. Running Flask/Werkzeug in debug mode exposes the interactive debugger and detailed tracebacks, enabling information disclosure and potential remote code execution.
SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False makes the session cookie accessible to JavaScript, so any XSS payload (e.g. the dashboard reflected XSS) can steal session tokens.

State-changing session-cookie-authenticated routes (/update_profile, /upload, /delete/<filename>) have no CSRF token validation and no CSRF library (Flask-WTF) is used anywhere in the project, allowing cross-site request forgery attacks against logged-in users.
print(session) in the /api/v1/update-profile handler writes the full Flask session object (username, user_id, session contents) to server logs, exposing sensitive session data.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The /api/v1/update_picture handler catches all exceptions and returns str(e) to the client with a 500 status, leaking internal error details (paths, library internals, request errors) that aid attackers.
